title: Console first screen: 1.1–1.8 s of main-thread script evaluation before LCP, mostly render work; cut first-render CPU
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA

Filing gate: maintainer ruling on #37444 at 2026-11-26 13:43Z (「先做最小一刀,其余立卡排队」: slice C rides #37444, the other seams queue as their own cards) · Source: fleet (production re-measure on #37444, comment 7193730951)

## What happens

Reading on a production build (method in #37444 comment 7193730951): script evaluation on the main thread is 1.1 s on Home and 1.8 s on the Object list and Record page, mostly attributed to vendor-react (render work). Even unthrottled and local, the observed LCP is already 2.0 / 2.6 / 2.5 s, and with bandwidth unlimited the list still sits at about 2.4–2.5 s. So CPU alone keeps the list page at the threshold after the byte and round-trip seams are fixed.

## Expected

- A profile of the first render on the three pages naming the components that dominate evaluation (re-renders during boot, large synchronous trees, work done before content paints).
- The biggest causes cut, so the list and record pages' unthrottled LCP drops clearly under 2.5 s.
- A pin on the fixed cause (render count or a timing budget a test can hold).
- Re-measure with the #37444 method and record the new medians there.

Not this card: eager JS size, the boot API waterfall, route lazy chunks (slice C, Part of #37444).

Related: #37444, #37398.

Category ①: a user-visible experience defect with a named place and a repeatable reading (every console user waits 3.6–4.6 s on the first screen).
Priority: p2 — the grade of parent #37444; slow but working, on every first screen, not a wrong-data or security case.
Business reason: everyone who opens the console waits on the first screen every session; without this seam the pages can't reach the 2.5 s threshold #37444 sets.
Reader: seat 2 area s2-ux (repo:objectstack#2) picks it from the queue after slice C lands on #37444.
Dedupe: `LCP console` 3 hits and `console render main thread first screen` 292 hits (top results read); the only open overlap is #37444 (the parent).
